variance_markers.label: A 4-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Sacramento State Hornets won the turnover battle by 4. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

variance_markers.label: A 21-point margin
variance_markers.text: Once a game is this far apart both teams stop playing the game they were rated on — the leader runs clock, the trailer throws — so late-game rates describe the situation rather than either team.

variance_markers.label: 1 non-offensive or return score
variance_markers.text: Points that arrived without an offensive drive. They count the same on the scoreboard and belong to a different distribution from the one the model prices.

verdict.line: No sportsbook quote was captured before publication, so there is no bet result to separate from the process. The reasoning is graded on its own below, which is the half that compounds.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk prices this game at Sacramento State +7.0 with a fair total of 48.0, which makes Kent State the better team here by that margin on this field.
lessons.actual_result: Kent State Golden Flashes lost by 21 where EdgeDesk projected a 7.1-point edge.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Kent State as better in market and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: Sacramento State Hornets won the game outright
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 7.1 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 9 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, continuity, special_teams.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: The model published an outcome range of -28.1 → +13.9 (Sacramento State).
lessons.actual_result: The game finished outside it, at a margin of 21.
lessons.lesson: The published range is meant to contain eight results in ten. A miss is expected roughly twice in ten games and is only a problem in aggregate — which is exactly what this store exists to measure.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Count range misses across the season. A rate materially above 20% means the model’s stated uncertainty is too narrow.
